web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: What future growth and margin durability is embedded in APARINDS's ₹61,411 Cr market cap at ₹14,667, and how does that compare to listed electrical and specialty-oil peers?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a cyclical-margin compounder is priced for permanent peak spreads, even a great business becomes a delicate stock.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: At the November 13, 2026 NSE close of ₹14,667.00, Apar Industries commands a ₹61,411.02 Cr market cap [21]. Trailing twelve-month (TTM) net profit stands at ₹1,377 Cr through September 2026, with TTM EPS at ₹338.29 [1]. The stock trades at 43.05x TTM P/E and 7.21x P/B on post-QIP book value [21]. On FY26 audited earnings (₹977 Cr PAT, ₹243.21 EPS), the trailing multiple is 60.3x [1].

Why does an industrial manufacturer earn a >40x trailing multiple? First, H1 FY27 delivered a sharp earnings jump. Q1 FY27 PAT rose to ₹467 Cr, and Q2 FY27 PAT reached ₹447 Cr [1]. Together, six-month profit hit ₹914 Cr, nearly matching all of FY26's ₹977 Cr [1]. Conductor EBITDA/MT surged to ₹48,241/MT, while Cable margins held above 10% [5, 6]. Second, the August 2026 ₹2,500 Cr QIP (16,88,618 shares) strengthened the balance sheet [10, 15]. Reserves jumped from ₹5,353 Cr to ₹8,478 Cr, cutting debt-to-equity to 0.12x [1, 21].

We run a 10-year Reverse DCF anchored to an enterprise value of roughly ₹60,400 Cr [1, 21]. That reflects ₹61,411 Cr market cap plus ₹1,020 Cr debt, net of post-QIP cash [1, 21]. We use an Indian industrial WACC of 11.5% (7.0% risk-free rate, 5.5% equity risk premium, 0.91 beta) and 5.0% terminal growth. From a normalized NOPAT base of ~₹1,450 Cr, today's price implies 19.5%–21.0% annual FCFF growth for ten years.

web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹14,667, the market prices in ~19.8% 10-year FCF compounding and ₹40,000+/MT conductor spreads. If spreads revert to ₹35,000–₹36,000/MT, near-term fair value compresses toward ₹12,800–₹13,500.

web_blocks.caption: APARINDS vs. Indian Electrical Cables & Specialty Oil Peers (Live Session Snapshot, 13 Nov 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: APARINDS trades at 43.05x TTM P/E—a 14%–18% premium to Polycab (37.8x) and KEI (36.6x), and 5.5x–7.3x higher than Gandhar (5.88x) and Savita Oil (7.81x). Its 31.8% ROCE rivals Polycab (33.2%), but leaves zero cushion for US tariff friction.

web_blocks.mechanism: Both European cable leaders saw multi-year EBITDA/MT expansion as offshore wind and HVDC interconnects created supply bottlenecks, lifting P/E multiples from 14x–16x to 22x–26x before project-timing pauses triggered 20%–30% pullbacks.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Prysmian grew EBITDA from €976M (2021) to >€1.9B (2024), yet suffered two 18%–25% valuation drawdowns whenever permitting slowed.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Even in a genuine grid supercycle, high-multiple industrials rarely move in a straight line; buying 43x TTM P/E invites sharp de-rating during any export pause.

web_blocks.html: Valuation Re-Rating Trigger: A pullback into the ₹13,300.78–₹13,705.88 zone drops the forward multiple to ~32x FY28E EPS (₹432) and lifts Base Target upside to +18.2%. Conversely, conductor EBITDA/MT falling below ₹35,000/MT would lower fair value toward ₹11,500.

web_blocks.title: Valuation Verdict: Great Business, Demanding Near-Term Multiple
paragraphs: Why does our 10-year Reverse DCF show ₹12,800 at 17% compounding while our 12–18 month Base Target is ₹16,200? The Reverse DCF discounts present intrinsic value today at an 11.5% WACC, whereas ₹16,200 values forward FY28E normalized EPS (₹432 at ₹37,000/MT conductor EBITDA) at 37.5x.

Under a Bear stress test—where Conductor EBITDA/MT reverts to management's ₹35,500/MT baseline midpoint (₹414 FY28E EPS) and P/E compresses to 30.0x—fair value drops to ₹12,420.00 (-15.32% from CMP). At CMP ₹14,667, upside to ₹16,200 is just +10.5%, too thin to buy above a broken 50-DMA.

book_paragraphs: Now that you and I have audited Apar Industries with the stock ticker taped over, let us peel back the tape and confront the market's price tag. As of the November 13, 2026 close, APARINDS trades at ₹14,667 per share, valuing the enterprise at ₹61,411 Cr—43.05 times trailing twelve-month earnings and 7.21 times post-QIP book value.

Pause and ask yourself the central question of Chapter 7: why would rational institutional buyers pay 43 times earnings for a company that still derives roughly a fifth of its revenue from transformer oils and a large chunk from aluminium conductors? Because the first half of FY27 changed the earnings trajectory. In just six months—Q1 and Q2 FY27—Apar generated ₹914 Cr of net profit, almost matching the entire ₹977 Cr it earned in all of FY26. When conductor EBITDA per metric ton jumps to ₹48,241 and the balance sheet is freshly fortified with ₹2,500 Cr of QIP equity, momentum investors extrapolate that run-rate into perpetuity.

That extrapolation is exactly what our Reverse DCF exposes. At an 11.5% cost of capital and 5% terminal growth, ₹14,667 implies that Apar must compound its free cash flow at nearly 20% a year for an entire decade. Look across the peer table: Polycab India, which boasts a higher 33.2% ROCE and a purer B2C/B2B cable mix, trades at 37.8x TTM earnings. KEI Industries trades at 36.6x. Meanwhile, pure-play transformer oil peers Gandhar Oil and Savita Oil trade at 5.9x and 7.8x. Apar is currently priced at a premium to every major domestic cable peer.

Does Apar deserve a premium to oil refiners? Unquestionably yes—its 31.8% ROCE, global UL/EN qualifications, and 45.8% premium conductor mix are in a different league. Does it deserve 43x trailing earnings if conductor spreads mean-revert toward management's own ₹35,000–₹36,000 per ton baseline? That is where discipline separates compounder investing from paying peak multiples.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a stock's price already embeds ~20% ten-year FCF compounding and ₹40,000+/MT conductor margins, you are no longer getting paid for the grid-electrification thesis—you are paying full retail for perfection. Patience for a better entry multiple is not timidity; it is arithmetic.

book_subsections.title: Normalized FY28E Valuation Bridge
paragraphs: If we model FY27E–FY28E conservatively—assuming Cable revenues compound at 22%+ as data-center and renewable orders execute, while Conductor EBITDA/MT cools from ₹48,241/MT back toward ₹37,000/MT—normalized FY28E EPS lands near ₹430 on the post-QIP 4.19 Cr share count. Applying a 37.5x exit multiple (in line with Polycab and KEI's current multiples) puts our 12–18 month Base Target at ₹16,200, Bull Target at ₹19,500, and Bear Target at ₹11,500.

At ₹14,667 today, the upside to ₹16,200 is just 10.5%. On a pullback into the ₹13,301–₹13,706 structural support zone, however, that same ₹16,200 target offers +18.2% to +21.8% upside against a tight -4.2% invalidation stop—a much healthier institutional risk-reward.

book_subsections.title: Peer Multiple Deconstruction: Why 43x TTM P/E Leaves Narrow Margin for Error
paragraphs: Let us walk through the peer comparison carefully so you can see where Apar Industries sits in the Indian market’s mental map. Polycab India, the undisputed leader in domestic wires and cables, trades at 37.8x trailing earnings on a 33.2% ROCE and 23.6% ROE. KEI Industries trades at 36.6x trailing earnings on a 20.0% ROCE. Havells India trades at 43.8x trailing earnings on a 24.9% ROCE, anchored by its consumer-facing switchgear and Lloyd appliance franchise. Meanwhile, pure-play transformer and specialty oil refiners—Gandhar Oil Refinery at 5.88x P/E and Savita Oil Technologies at 7.81x P/E—trade at single-digit multiples because oil refining carries thinner margins and lower terminal growth.

Where does Apar sit? At ₹14,667, Apar trades at 43.05x trailing earnings—higher than both Polycab and KEI, and virtually identical to Havells—even though roughly a fifth of Apar’s revenue still comes from Transformer and Specialty Oils and another half comes from Conductors. Why? Because the market is treating Apar’s Q1 and Q2 FY27 earnings burst (₹914 Cr combined PAT in six months, powered by ₹48,241/MT conductor EBITDA and 10%+ cable margins) as a permanent structural plateau rather than a cyclical high-water mark. If conductor spreads settle back toward management’s ₹35,000–₹36,000/MT long-term baseline while Cables continue compounding at 20%+, Apar remains a superb long-term compounder, but paying 43x trailing earnings leaves almost no cushion for a single quarter of US tariff friction or project-delivery delay.

That is also the lesson of our European grid parallel, Prysmian S.p.A. and Nexans. During the 2021–2025 offshore wind and HVDC supercycle, Prysmian expanded EBITDA from €976 million to over €1.9 billion and re-rated sharply, yet the stock still endured two 18%–25% valuation drawdowns whenever permitting slowed or quarterly mix softened. Great grid franchises do not move in straight lines—and neither should your entry price.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing the Valuation Against Base-Rate Cyclicality
paragraphs: Let us test one more angle before leaving valuation: what happens if we are slightly too conservative on Cable growth, or slightly too optimistic on Conductor spreads? Our Reverse DCF matrix makes the trade-off transparent. If Apar compounds NOPAT at 14% annually over the next decade—consistent with conductor EBITDA/MT normalizing to ₹33,000–₹35,000/MT—intrinsic value drops toward ₹9,995 per share, representing over 31% downside from ₹14,667. At 17% compounding (₹36,000–₹38,000/MT conductor EBITDA), fair value sits near ₹12,800.

Only if Apar sustains 19.8%–22.5% ten-year FCF compounding and holds conductor margins above ₹40,000–₹44,000/MT does today’s ₹14,667 price look cheap—pointing toward ₹17,790–₹19,500. That is why waiting for a pullback into the ₹13,301–₹13,706 support zone transforms the bet: you shift the entry point down toward base-case intrinsic value while keeping full upside to the grid supercycle.
